newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bezeq says India cellular venture begins.
newsitem.headline: Bezeq says India cellular venture begins.

text.p: Bezeq Israel Telecom Ltd said on Tuesday that its Indian cellular telephone joint venture had provided more than 2,000 lines since it began commercial operations more than two weeks ago.

"Bezeq...received a telegram of congratulations from the mananging director of Fascel, Mr Atip Rittaporn, in which he announced 'our companies launched the commercial service in the Gujarat district to provide cellular service to the district residents'," Bezeq said in a statement.

Fascel is a joint venture between India's Himachal Futuristic Communications Ltd (HFCL), in which Bezeq holds a 49 percent stake, Shinawatra of Thailand, the Indian finance company Kotak Mahindra and Indusind of the Hindujas Corp.
Bezeq said Fascel began commercial operations in the Inidian state of Gujarat at the end of January. The first lines were for subscribers in the state's capital city of Ahmadabad and surroundings.
"This March, the company will provide phones in other areas of the district," it said. Gujarat has some 43 million inhabitants.

Fascel, which uses GSM cellular technology, provides the service under the name Celforce. It is one of two joint ventures Bezeq has in India. The second, also with HFCL, won tenders for wireline phone service in nine of India's 21 telephone zones, but that project has run into difficulties.
